text:
Maya (Finance): quick flag - our week-over-week subsidiary totals are off. Found ~95 Stripe invoices posted into NetSuite with USD/US subsidiary but the customers are EU. Likely related to Friday's email normalizer rollout.

Priya (Revenue Ops): I noticed the variance in export totals this morning. Which connector did we change? Email normalization - lowercasing + strip subdomains?

Connor (Billing Eng): yes, we pushed the email normalizer to canonicalize addresses (strip+lower). It inadvertently removed the country tag for some corporate domains like corp.acme.eu -> acme.eu and our legacy resolver used subdomain hints. Fuzzy resolver then matched to the US record.

Maya (Finance): That will break VAT/tax codes and exchange rates. Month close is in 6 days. We need a remediation plan that doesn't blow up the GL.

Connor (Billing Eng): first step I can do a read-only audit to list affected invoices and the delta per subsidiary. Draft query I'll run against the sync logs: 
```
SELECT s.invoice_id, s.customer_email, s.currency, s.amount_cents, match.subsidiary as matched_sub, match.confidence, cust.expected_subsidiary
FROM sync_events s
JOIN customer_matches match ON match.stripe_customer = s.customer_id
JOIN customers cust ON cust.stripe_customer = s.customer_id
WHERE s.gateway = 'stripe' AND s.event_type = 'invoice.created'
AND s.timestamp >= '2026-03-20';
```

OpsBot: 3 webhook failures in last 48h for stripe->ns-sync. DLQ messages: dlq_a12, dlq_b34, dlq_c56. No auto-replay configured.

Elena (Accounting): For remediation I prefer: reverse the posted NS invoice (create credit memo), then recreate properly under the right subsidiary. Keeps audit trail. Avoids journal gymnastics.

Nora (Legal): if we reissue invoices across jurisdictions, check contractual language about tax handling and notify customers if VAT charges change. We might need a customer-communication plan.

Priya (Revenue Ops): Also check subscriptions with proration events - if we reverse/reissue we shouldn't break usage-based billing records. Connor can we keep Stripe IDs linked?

Connor (Billing Eng): yes, plan is to preserve Stripe invoice id in a custom field on the new NetSuite invoice and tag the old one with redwood:correction:2026-03-24. That way accounting can reconcile.

Maya (Finance): timeline? We need the list and estimated GL impact by tomorrow EOD. If it's >250 invoices we need director-level approval to run automated fixes.

Connor (Billing Eng): I'll run the audit now and post a CSV to #finance-private. CSV will include columns: stripe_invoice, stripe_customer, current_ns_id, current_sub, expected_sub, amount, currency, tax_code, suggested_fix (reverse+recreate | journal), estimated_gl_change, notes.

Priya (Revenue Ops): Can you also add a column for subscription_id and proration_flag so we can triage subscriptions vs one-off invoices?

Connor (Billing Eng): will do. Dry-run will be read-only, promise.

OpsBot: monthly_exports job scheduled Wed 06:00 UTC. Recommendation: pause exports during remediation to prevent duplicate downstream processing.

Elena (Accounting): Once we have CSV I'll sample 10 invoices for manual review. If small counts, we can do manual fixes. If medium-large, automated reversal+recreate with double-checks.

Maya (Finance): Also include timeframe cutoff: which created_at range to consider. We might limit to post-deploy window (Fri 22:00 UTC -> now).

Connor (Billing Eng): good call. I'll scope to deploy window and include a confidence score from fuzzy matcher so we can filter high-risk. Example log sample: 
```
--- match sample ---
stripe_inv: inv_7Zxy9, cust: cus_H9k, email: billing@Acme.EU -> normalized: billing@acme.eu
legacy_hint: corp.acme.eu (was used for EU) -> removed by normalizer
matcher: acme.com (score 0.82) -> selected US subsidiary
expected: acme.eu (score 0.99)
```

Priya (Revenue Ops): Can we temporarily revert normalizer config or add an override that preserves subdomain tokens for corporate domains?

Connor (Billing Eng): I can quickly roll back the normalizer or add a whitelist. But rolling back risks reintroducing other duplicate-customer issues. Prefer to keep change and fix the mis-matches programmatically.

Nora (Legal): If rollback reduces risk of cross-border invoicing mistakes this week, consider it as a stop-gap. Notify ops and revenue before revert.

Maya (Finance): Let's proceed: 1) Connor do dry-run audit and CSV by EOD tomorrow. 2) If affected invoices <= 200, prefer automated reversal+recreate in weekend window; if >200, escalate for manual approval. 3) Pause monthly exports during remediation. 4) Legal to review customer comms if needed.

Connor (Billing Eng): ack. I'll include suggested window (Sunday 02:00-05:00 UTC), idempotency keys, changelog writes, and a rollback plan that reverts tags and re-posts originals if anything fails.

Priya (Revenue Ops): Please also add a smoke test: compare gross totals by subsidiary pre/post and run sample reconciliation for top 10 customers.

OpsBot: Alert: export job paused flag set to false by default. Admin action required to pause.

Elena (Accounting): approve dry-run. Hold on programmatic run until CSV review.

Maya (Finance): thanks all. Connor - post CSV here and ping infra to prepare throttled runner if we go automated.

Connor (Billing Eng): will do. Posting in #finance-private once done. Will update this thread when CSV is uploaded.
